terra.problem: “Same army” assumes Benaiah was in David’s army at the time of this scene. The cited verse describes a later time.
The passage does not say neither king was at the pool. Identifying both men as kings also needs a reference outside this passage.
The text does not say both sides stay exactly where they are after Abner’s suggestion.
Saying whoever counted the men made sure the sides were equal adds an intention the text does not give.
The explanation repeats the equal count without adding much. It is flat for a moment that could carry some personality.
The explanation repeats the count and comparison without much personality or a worthwhile laugh.
Calling what follows “the real fighting” diminishes the deadly violence of the contest.
Calling Abner the commander on the other side needs a reference; that role is not stated in this passage.
The passage does not state that Ish-bosheth was absent from the battlefield. His kingship also needs a reference outside this passage.
The text does not say the Benjamites had been running or that they turned around together.
The text says the pursuers had reached a place by sunset, not that sunset had already come before the chase stopped.
“One horn blast” adds a number of blasts the text does not give.
The text identifies the tomb as belonging to Asahel’s father, but does not say his father is buried there or that Bethlehem was Asahel’s home.
The text does not say Bethlehem was Asahel’s home.
Saying Saul’s side is “shrinking” suggests a decrease in size. The text says it grew weaker.
